Myopia is one of the most common vision conditions worldwide, and this video helps viewers understand the real-life challenges millions of people face daily when they don’t have corrective lenses. 🧐

caption:
😅
Not doing anything at work can feel strangely exhausting, even though it involves very little effort. Time seems to move more slowly when there are no tasks to focus on, and sitting idle can make a day feel unproductive and unfulfilling. Without clear responsibilities, it’s easy for boredom to creep in, leading to restlessness and a lack of motivation. For many people, the absence of meaningful work can be more draining than a busy schedule.
At the same time, periods of doing nothing at work can reveal deeper issues, such as poor management, unclear expectations, or inefficient workflows. When employees are underutilized, it can affect morale and long-term engagement, making people feel disconnected from their roles. However, these moments can also be opportunities for reflection, learning, or planning ahead if used intentionally. How that idle time is handled often determines whether it becomes wasted time or a chance for growth.

hook: The Visionary Behind Amazon's Empire
caption:
The Visionary Behind Amazon's Empire
Jeffrey Preston Bezos, born on January 12, 1964, in Albuquerque, New Mexico, is an American entrepreneur, investor, and space enthusiast best known as the founder of Amazon.com. Starting his career in finance on Wall Street, Bezos left a high-paying job in 1994 to launch an online bookstore from his garage-a risky move that would change the world of commerce forever.
Under his leadership, Amazon evolved from a small book-selling website into one of the largest and most influential tech companies globally, revolutionizing e-commerce, cloud computing (through AWS), digital media, and logistics. His obsession with customer satisfaction, innovation, and long-term thinking earned him a reputation as one of the most forward-thinking CEOs of his time.

Most limits exist only because no one questions the pace they were set at
Elon Musk believes that almost everything we do is slower than it needs to be. Whatever speed a process is running at today, it can be pushed further if someone is willing to challenge assumptions and rethink how it is done. Progress stalls when people accept the current tempo as fixed.
By constantly asking how something can be done faster, Musk forces teams to remove unnecessary steps and outdated rules. This mindset turns speed itself into a competitive advantage and is often what separates breakthrough companies from average ones.
